text:
nina: We're seeing sporadic OOMs on the new aurora-lite13b-int4 rollout. Traces point to allocator fragmentation after ~3h under steady traffic. Mostly long-chat sessions (>700 tokens).
omar: Interesting. Is memory_tiling enabled and what's prefetch_window/prefetch_bias? Could be hoarding.
nina: Yes memory_tiling=true. Config: max_new_tokens=1500, batching.max_concurrent=6, prefetch_window=80, memory_tiling.prefetch_bias=0.85.
lee: That bias is super aggressive for int4. Suggest drop bias and clamp max_new_tokens. For initial warmup use: prefetch_bias=0.45, max_new_tokens=300, batching.max_concurrent=2.
tess: Also enable `kv_trim_threshold=0.55` and `soft_evict=true` so we reclaim without hard drops. Add `slot_reserve=0.06` to allocation policy.
omar: For safety add per-route `client_max_tokens=1024` and server side `per_request.kv_eviction=on-epoch`. Long-lived requests are the main culprit.
nina: rolled a quick canary to 3 nodes with prefetch_bias=0.45, max_new_tokens=300, batching.max_concurrent=2, slot_reserve=0.06.
deploy-bot: deploy 6189991234 by nina to eng-dedicated-canary at 2024-11-06T09:03:12Z — success
lee: run a short regression eval on our longform-story dataset (50 samples). Check Rouge-L and exact-match for code blocks. If int4 delta >1.2% hold.
tess: Also snapshot slab allocator histograms and free-slot distributions before/after a 6h run. That will show whether fragmentation reduces.
omar: FYI I saw similar pattern on bach-14b-int4 where lowering prefetch_window from 128->48 fixed churn. Could be window+bias interaction. Keep an eye on prefetch_window too.
nina: noted — will try prefetch_window=48 if churn persists. Starting 24h canary run and eval job. Ill post metrics in ~3h. :eyes:
